call_points.text: Management declined to give any forward volume or market-share number for FY27, tracking member, FPI and co-location counts instead.
ICCL took an ECL provision on an old ₹80 Cr outstanding from NSE, which raised Q4 other expenses.
call_points.versus_prior: answers the Q4 other expenses trend flagged for Q1FY27 results

call_points.text: FY26 derivatives average daily premium turnover reached ₹19,523 Cr, up 118% from ₹8,978 Cr in FY25.
call_points.versus_prior: extends the transaction-charge surge noted in the Q4FY26 call

call_points.text: Monthly contracts are still only 5-6% of volumes; management wants more long-term participants to lift them.
Member count rose from 446 to 587 in a year, FPIs from 100 to 520, and co-location racks from 300 to 500.
Co-location revenue rose to ₹171 Cr in FY26 from ₹74 Cr, helped by the revised Throttle Charges Framework of July 2025.
Technology budget of about ₹300 Cr may nearly double as memory and hardware prices rise.
Clearing expense is tied to contract count while revenue is tied to premium, so the two cannot be predicted together.
Commodity derivatives are being explored but no timeline or cost was given.
Transaction charges surged significantly driven by strong growth in equity and derivative segments.

operating_notes.text: Regulatory contribution was the largest cost line at ₹64,969 lakh in FY26, against ₹41,046 lakh in FY25.
The group operates in one business segment, facilitating trading in securities and related ancillary services.
An incremental gratuity expense of ₹1,301 lakh was recognised for FY26 on the new Labour Codes.
FY26 derivatives average daily premium turnover was ₹19,523 Cr, up 118% from ₹8,978 Cr in FY25.
FY26 co-location revenue was ₹171 Cr against ₹74 Cr in FY25.
Monthly contracts were 5-6% of derivatives volumes; FPI participation was 5-6% against a market level of around 9%.
